exam.title: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examinations 2024 - Agriculture (4128)

questions.stem: Which of the following irrigation system minimizes wastage of water?
explanation_steps: Drip irrigation is the most efficient system because it delivers water directly to the root zone of the plant in small, frequent amounts. This significantly reduces losses due to evaporation and runoff compared to surface methods like spate or basin irrigation.

questions.stem: All the following are biotic constraints that reduce agricultural production, **except**
explanation_steps: Biotic factors are living organisms that affect agriculture. Weeds, diseases (bacteria/fungi), insects, and rodents are all living organisms. **Low rainfall** is an abiotic (non-living) environmental factor.

questions.stem: The black cotton soil that is found in the south western lowland of Eritrea is
explanation_steps: Vertisols are heavy clay soils, often dark in color, that expand when wet and crack deeply when dry. They are commonly known as 'black cotton soils' and are prevalent in the southwestern lowlands of Eritrea.

questions.stem: Among the following crops which group are used for raw materials in textile industry?
explanation_steps: Textile industries require fiber crops. Cotton, flax, and jute are all grown primarily for their fibers which are used to make clothes, linen, and bags. Barley and sorghum are food crops (cereals).

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** a component of modern agriculture?
explanation_steps: Modern agriculture relies on mechanization (tractors, combine harvesters) and biotechnology (improved breeds and seeds). Hunting and gathering wild fruits are primitive methods used before the invention of settled agriculture.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** a correct statement about the importance of humus in agriculture?

options.A: It is a by-product of organic matter decomposition.
options.B: It helps in holding cations in the soil.
options.C: It has less water holding capacity.
options.E: It is compost extracted from forest components.

explanation_steps: Humus is highly beneficial because it **increases** the water-holding capacity of the soil. Statement C is incorrect because it claims humus has 'less' capacity.

questions.stem: The agricultural science that studies forage and pasture is
explanation_steps: While forage is a plant, its study is often integrated into Animal Science because it focuses on the nutrition and feeding of livestock. In many contexts, this specifically falls under Range Management or Animal Nutrition.

questions.stem: In soil science, an instrument that is used to determine matric water potential is called
explanation_steps: A tensiometer measures the moisture tension in the soil, which is an indicator of how hard the plant roots have to work to extract water. This is formally known as 'matric potential'.

questions.stem: One of the following **is not** a major element of climate?
explanation_steps: The elements of climate are measurable atmospheric conditions like temperature, rainfall, and humidity. **Topography** (the physical features of the land like mountains) is a factor that *influences* climate, but it is not an element of climate itself.

questions.stem: All of the following are negative impacts of agricultural practices, **except**

options.A: soil contamination from inappropriate use of inorganic fertilizers.
options.B: air pollution due to the use of insecticides.
options.C: clearing of forest area for crop cultivation.

explanation_steps: Soil and land reclamation is a positive agricultural practice aimed at restoring damaged land or creating new land for productive use. The other options describe degradation or pollution.

questions.stem: All of the following are essential and major plant nutrients, **except**
explanation_steps: Plant nutrients are divided into macronutrients (needed in large amounts) and micronutrients (needed in trace amounts). Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), and Magnesium (Mg) are all macronutrients. **Manganese (Mn)** is a micronutrient.

questions.stem: Identify the camel breed which is widely known in Eritrea.
explanation_steps: The Adali camel is a prominent breed in Eritrea, particularly among the Afar people in the Southern Red Sea region. It is well-adapted to harsh, arid conditions.

questions.stem: The type of soil that has diameter size $$ < 0.002 $$ mili meter is
explanation_steps: Soil particles are classified by size. Sand particles are the largest, silt is medium, and **clay** particles are the smallest, with a diameter less than 0.002 mm.

questions.stem: The perennial river basin that flows northwards forming the border between Eritrea and Ethiopia is
explanation_steps: The Setit (also known as Tekeze in Ethiopia) is the only perennial river (flows all year round) that forms part of the southwestern border between Eritrea and Ethiopia.

questions.stem: One of the following crops **is not** included in the Abyssinian Centre of Diversity.
explanation_steps: The Abyssinian (Ethiopian/Eritrean) Highlands is a center of origin for crops like coffee, teff, sorghum, and barley. **Maize (Corn)** originated in Central America (Mexico) and was introduced to Africa much later.

questions.stem: Among the following, identify the crop that performs well in hot season conditions.
explanation_steps: Sorghum is a drought-tolerant C4 plant that grows exceptionally well in hot, semi-arid conditions. Cabbage, wheat, barley, and lentils prefer cooler highland temperatures.

questions.stem: A researcher conducted an experiment on field crop with plot size of $$ 4\\text{m} \\times 3\\text{m} $$ and used $$ 18\\text{ gm.} $$ of seeds for this plot. What is the seed rate per hectare?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Calculate plot area: $$ 4\\text{m} \\times 3\\text{m} = 12\\text{ m}^2 $$.
**Step 2:** Find seed rate per $$ 1\\text{ m}^2 $$: $$ 18\\text{ g} / 12\\text{ m}^2 = 1.5\\text{ g/m}^2 $$.
**Step 3:** Convert to hectare ($$ 1\\text{ ha} = 10,000\\text{ m}^2 $$): $$ 1.5\\text{ g} \\times 10,000 = 15,000\\text{ g} $$.
**Step 4:** Convert to kg: $$ 15,000\\text{ g} / 1000 = 15\\text{ kg/ha} $$.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements **is not** beneficial feature of weeds?

options.A: Can serve as a source of animal feed
options.B: Can be used as a source of medicinal values
options.E: Can serve for soil and water conservation

explanation_steps: Weeds are generally harmful, but they can have minor benefits like animal feed or medicinal use. **Harbouring insects and diseases** is a major **disadvantage** of weeds because it puts the main crop at risk.

questions.stem: A potential fatal mammary gland, in livestock, caused due to infections and inflammations of the udder tissue is
explanation_steps: Mastitis is the inflammation of the mammary gland (udder) usually caused by bacterial infection. It is a serious condition in dairy cows that reduces milk quality and can be fatal if not treated.

questions.stem: Green foliage of crops preserved and fermented in underground containers for use as animal feed is
explanation_steps: Silage is high-moisture stored fodder which can be fed to cattle and sheep. It is made by preserving green crops (like maize or sorghum) through fermentation in anaerobic conditions (without air), often in pits or silos.

questions.stem:
The agro-ecological zone denoted by number "1" is

![Agro-ecological zones of Eritrea](file:///android_asset/exam_images/agr_2024_q21_1.webp)
explanation_steps: Based on the provided map of Eritrea's agro-ecological zones, number '1' represents the Southwestern Lowlands. This region is characterized as Arid Lowland due to its high temperatures and seasonal rainfall patterns.

questions.stem:
The major crop grown in the agro-ecological zone denoted by number "2" is

![Agro-ecological zones of Eritrea](file:///android_asset/exam_images/agr_2024_q21_1.webp)
explanation_steps: Zone '2' represents the Central Highlands of Eritrea. Highland areas have cooler climates suitable for temperate crops. Barley, wheat, and teff are the dominant crops in this zone. Sesame, cotton, and pearl millet are lowland crops.

questions.stem:
The second largest agro-ecological zone in Eritrea is indicated by

![Agro-ecological zones of Eritrea](file:///android_asset/exam_images/agr_2024_q21_1.webp)
explanation_steps: In terms of total land area in Eritrea, the Semi-desert zone (indicated by number 3, covering the coastal strip) is the largest or second largest. Most official sources list the Northwestern Lowlands (4) and the Semi-desert (3) as the two largest zones by area.

questions.stem: During photosynthesis, which portion of the electromagnetic spectrum is most absorbed by the chlorophyll?
explanation_steps: Chlorophyll, the green pigment in plants, absorbs light most efficiently in the blue-violet and red parts of the visible spectrum. It reflects green light, which is why leaves appear green to our eyes.

questions.stem: All of the following are monocot types of plants, except
explanation_steps: Monocots (monocotyledons) have one seed leaf (e.g., grasses and cereals like taff, wheat, barley, maize). Dicots have two seed leaves. Faba bean is a legume, which is a **dicot**.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not** true about the advantages of row planting.
explanation_steps: Row planting is more efficient than broadcasting. One of its main benefits is that it **reduces** the amount of seed needed because seeds are placed precisely. Therefore, option E is incorrect.

questions.stem: Which of the following manures give higher nitrogen source?
explanation_steps: Poultry manure (bird droppings) is known to have the highest nitrogen content among animal manures. It is highly concentrated and effective for boosting plant growth, though it must be handled carefully to avoid 'burning' plants.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions lead to poor seed germination?
explanation_steps: For a seed to germinate properly, it needs to be healthy and intact. Shrivelled, broken, wrinkled, or undersized seeds often lack enough stored food (endosperm) or have damaged embryos, resulting in poor or no growth.

questions.stem: One of the following **is not** a vegetative propagation method of plants.
explanation_steps: Vegetative propagation is asexual reproduction using plant parts (stems, roots, leaves). Cutting, layering, budding, and grafting are all asexual methods. **Seeding** involves seeds, which are products of sexual reproduction.

questions.stem: The first cow milk produced after giving birth to a calf is
explanation_steps: Colostrum is the first form of milk produced by the mammary glands immediately following delivery of the newborn. It is thick, yellowish, and rich in antibodies (immunoglobulins) which are critical for the survival of the calf.

questions.stem: During seed bed preparation, the use of raised seed beds is important to
explanation_steps: Raised seed beds are elevated above the ground level. Their primary purpose is to improve soil drainage and aeration, preventing waterlogging which can rot sensitive seeds and young seedlings.

questions.stem: A type of animal feed which provides good source of concentrate is
explanation_steps: Concentrates are feeds that are high in energy and/or protein but low in fiber. Oil-seed cakes (the byproduct of oil extraction from seeds like sesame or cotton) are excellent protein concentrates.

questions.stem: ________ is the act of separating/ stopping a young suckling goat from its mother.
explanation_steps: Weaning is the process of gradually introducing a young mammal to what will be its adult diet while withdrawing the supply of its mother's milk.

questions.stem: The highest population of livestock in Eritrea are
explanation_steps: In Eritrea, goats are the most numerous livestock because they are highly adaptable to various climates, from the dry lowlands to the rugged highlands, and can graze on sparse vegetation.

questions.stem: Identify the **incorrect** statement on the importance of mulching.
explanation_steps: Mulching involves covering the soil surface with organic or inorganic materials. It **minimizes** weed growth by blocking sunlight. Therefore, saying it 'increases' weed infestation is incorrect.

questions.stem: Which one of the following cattle breed is indigenous to Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The Arado cattle (often found in the highlands) and the Begait/Barka cattle (found in the lowlands) are the primary indigenous breeds of Eritrea. Holstein, Jersey, and Ayrshire are exotic breeds from Europe.

questions.stem: All of the following are essential amino acids that need to be provided in the diet for optimum performance of domestic animals, **except**
explanation_steps: Essential amino acids are those an animal cannot synthesize on its own and must eat. For most monogastric animals, Proline is considered a non-essential amino acid because the body can produce enough of it.

questions.stem: A system of grazing practiced in high potential production areas in which a rope or a chain is used to confine the animal within a limited pasture area is called
explanation_steps: Tethering is the practice of tying an animal to a fixed object or a stake with a rope or chain so it can graze in a specific, limited area. This is common where land is scarce or crops are nearby.

questions.stem: The ________ prevents particles of sand or gravel from getting into the digestive system of chicken.
explanation_steps: The gizzard is a muscular stomach in birds. It actually *uses* sand and small stones (grit) to grind down tough food particles. While the question asks what 'prevents' them from moving further, the gizzard is the specific organ where these particles are retained to function as 'teeth'.

questions.stem: Which of the following animal traits **is most** suitable for selection?
explanation_steps: Selection is the process of choosing the best animals to be parents of the next generation. Farmers look for productive traits (milk), health traits (disease resistance), and physical traits (udder size) to improve their herd.

questions.stem: One of the following vegetation types is **not** found at high elevation areas.
explanation_steps: Mangrove forests are coastal vegetation types that grow in saline or brackish water in intertidal zones (where the land meets the sea). They are never found at high elevations (mountains).

questions.stem: In pest management, biological control involves the use of
explanation_steps: Biological control is a method of controlling pests (insects, mites, weeds) using other organisms. It relies on natural predation, parasitism, or herbivory—essentially using 'natural enemies' like ladybugs to eat aphids.

questions.stem: All of the following are common ecto-parasitic infestations in animals, **except**
explanation_steps: Ecto-parasites live on the *outside* of the host's body (skin/hair). Ticks, mites, fleas, and lice are all external. **Flukes** (like liver flukes) are endo-parasites because they live *inside* the animal's organs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the largest reservoir in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Kerkebet Dam, located on the Anseba River, is the largest strategic water reservoir in Eritrea. It has a massive capacity intended for large-scale agricultural projects in the Gash-Barka region.

questions.stem: ________ is a preventive measure used to control animal diseases by separating seemingly healthy animals exposed to the risk of infection.
explanation_steps: Quarantine is the practice of isolating animals that have arrived from another farm or have been exposed to a disease, even if they look healthy, to see if they develop symptoms before joining the main herd.

questions.stem: Which of the following tree species is mainly found in the riverine areas, along the Gash Barka river?
explanation_steps: *Hyphaenae thebaica*, commonly known as the Dom Palm (Ak'at), is the iconic tree species found along the seasonal riverbanks (riverine areas) of the Barka and Gash rivers in Eritrea.

questions.stem: One of the following is prominent invasive plant species in Eritrea.
explanation_steps: *Prosopis juliflora*, locally known as 'Temer-musa', is a highly invasive woody weed in Eritrea. It spreads rapidly, chokes out native vegetation, and can make land unusable for grazing.

questions.stem: Which of the following livestock was domesticated, mainly, as draught-power?
explanation_steps: Draught animals are kept for their physical strength to pull loads or farm equipment (plowing). Horses and Donkeys (and Oxen) are primary draught animals. Pigs, sheep, and goats are kept for meat, milk, or wool.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is correct** about the causes of wildlife decline in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Eritrea's wildlife faces multiple threats. Over-hunting, the spread of invasive species that compete with local animals, illegal trade, and the destruction of forests/habitats for farming all contribute to the decline of species like lions, elephants, and wild asses.

questions.stem: The parasitic weed, *Striga hermonthica* that attacks sorghum can mostly be controlled by
explanation_steps: *Striga* (Witchweed) thrives in soils with low fertility. Adding organic manure improves soil health and suppresses the weed. Crop rotation breaks the weed's life cycle. **Mono-cropping** (growing sorghum every year) actually makes the Striga problem **worse**.

questions.stem: All of the following are reasons for the decline of forests in Eritrea, **except**
explanation_steps: Forest decline is caused by cutting wood, expanding farms, and overgrazing. **Establishment of enclosures** is a conservation strategy used to *protect* and restore forests by fencing them off from people and livestock. Therefore, it is the only positive action listed.

questions.stem: One of the following is a **disadvantage** of growing seedlings in containers.

options.B: They require regular root pruning in the nursery.
options.C: The roots are not exposed to air-drying during lifting.
options.D: Good soil at the nursery site is not an essential requirement.
options.E: They require less space in the nursery.

explanation_steps: Growing seedlings in pots or containers is efficient, but if the seedlings stay too long, their roots will spiral around the container. This requires **regular root pruning**, which is an extra labor-intensive maintenance task (a disadvantage).

questions.stem: The following are contributions of soil and water conservation, **except**

options.A: increases organic matter in the soil.

explanation_steps: Soil and water conservation is meant to **prevent** or reduce soil loss (erosion). Therefore, saying it 'increases soil losses' is completely opposite to its purpose.

questions.stem: Which of the following human activities **does not** cause chemical soil degradation?

options.A: Use of heavy machines on agricultural fields.
options.C: Improper use of fertilizer levels and amount.
options.D: Loss of nutrients and organic matter.
options.E: Fixing of soluble nutrients under alkaline soil condition.

explanation_steps: Chemical degradation involves changes in the soil's chemistry (salinity, pH, nutrients). **Using heavy machines** causes **physical degradation** (soil compaction and destruction of soil structure), not chemical change.

questions.stem: The cropping system in which perennial trees are integrated with annuals is called
explanation_steps: Agro-forestry is a land management system where trees or shrubs (perennials) are grown around or among crops (annuals) or pastureland. It combines agriculture and forestry technologies.

questions.stem: Which one of the following **is not** an alternative renewable energy source?
explanation_steps: Renewable energy comes from sources that don't run out (Sun, Wind, Water). **Fossil fuels** (coal, oil, natural gas) are non-renewable because they take millions of years to form and will eventually be exhausted.

questions.stem: Which of the following environmental factors are affecting the regeneration of tree species in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Tree regeneration depends on both abiotic factors (Light for photosynthesis, Moisture for seeds to sprout, Nutrients for growth) and biotic factors (Animals, which can either disperse seeds or destroy young saplings by grazing).

questions.stem: All of the following factors affect the rate and extent of soil degradation, **except**
explanation_steps: Relief, slope, land use intensity, and climate are all factors that can **increase** degradation. **Minimum tillage** (disturbing the soil as little as possible) is a management practice designed to **prevent** degradation.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is **incorrect** about trees?

options.C: They provide shade and wildlife habitat.
options.E: They are net carbon dioxide emitters.

explanation_steps: Trees are 'Carbon Sinks', meaning they absorb carbon dioxide ($$CO_2$$) for photosynthesis and release oxygen. They are **not** net emitters of $$CO_2$$; they help reduce it in the atmosphere.

questions.stem: The life style of individual living populations in a given habitat is referred to as
explanation_steps: An ecological **niche** is the specific role or 'lifestyle' of an organism or population within its community, including its habitat, what it eats, and how it survives.

questions.stem: Semenawi-Bahri is a national protected area for which wildlife conservation?
explanation_steps: Semenawi-Bahri (The Green Belt) is a protected area in Eritrea known for its unique coniferous and broadleaf forests. It provides a habitat for various wildlife, most notably the **Greater Kudu**, as well as leopards and diverse bird species. Wild Asses are found in the Danakil, and Elephants in Gash-Setit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an indicator of successful farm management systems?

options.A: Planning and purchase of inputs and combining them in production.
options.B: Timely decision on the types of crops and livestock to be produced.
options.C: Planning and coordinating of activities in the farming enterprise.
options.D: Bearing all consequences on risks and successes concerning the farm enterprise.

explanation_steps: Successful farm management involves a combination of planning, timely decision-making, coordination, and risk management. A farmer must decide what to grow, how to manage resources, and accept the financial outcomes of their decisions.

questions.stem: One of the following **is not** a method of replenishing soil nutrients in agriculture.

options.B: Use of animal dung for fuel

explanation_steps: To replenish soil nutrients, you must add organic or inorganic matter back into the soil. **Using animal dung for fuel** (burning it for cooking) removes potential nutrients from the farm system instead of returning them to the soil. Manure, fertilizers, and nitrogen fixation all add nutrients.

questions.stem: An/ A ________ is a line joining points on the same elevation either on the ground or on a map.
explanation_steps: A **contour line** (or just a contour) is a line on a map that joins points of equal elevation above sea level. This is essential for understanding the topography and planning soil conservation structures like terraces.

questions.stem: Which of the following is different from the others?
explanation_steps: Centre pivot irrigation is a **modern, pressurized** irrigation system that uses machinery and pumps to spray water. All the other options (Spate, Flood, Basin, Furrow) are **surface/gravitational** methods that rely on water flowing over the ground.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of erosion **is not** commonly observed in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Glacial erosion is caused by the movement of glaciers (ice). Since Eritrea is a tropical country and does not have glaciers, this type of erosion is not observed. Water (Rill, Gully, Sheet) and wind erosion are the major types in Eritrea.

questions.stem: All of the following are common problems in the field of farm management and planning in Eritrea, **except**

options.B: the nature of the farm enterprises follow traditional farming method.
options.C: inadequate capital and slow adoption of innovations.
options.D: high managerial skills and existence of good market outlets.

explanation_steps: Small farm sizes, traditional methods, lack of money (capital), and poor supply chains are all major **challenges** (problems) for Eritrean farmers. **High managerial skills and good markets** are positive factors (strengths), not problems.

questions.stem: Hand-held instrument used to quickly measure percentage slope and gradients is
explanation_steps: A clinometer is a small, hand-held tool used to measure angles of slope, elevation, or depression of an object with respect to gravity. It is used in farming to determine how steep a hillside is.

questions.stem: Identify the **incorrect** statement regarding the characteristics of agricultural products in Eritrea.

options.C: The prices of agricultural products are relatively unstable.
options.D: Poor input and output market linkage and information.

explanation_steps: All the statements (A, B, C, D) are actually true characteristics of the current agricultural situation in Eritrea. Products come all at once (seasonal), they rot quickly (perishable), prices jump up and down, and market info is hard to find. Since all are true, none are 'incorrect'.

questions.stem: All the following contribute to poor soil drainage, **except**

options.A: too much rainfall during the rainy season.
options.B: existence of high clay content in the soil.
options.C: limestone lies above an impermeable clay layer.
options.D: existence of high organic matter decomposition.
options.E: hard pans in clay contents are found in the sub-soil.

explanation_steps: Poor drainage happens when water cannot move through the soil. Clay and hard-pans block water. However, **organic matter decomposition** (humus) **improves** soil structure and porosity, which actually **helps** drainage instead of making it poor.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is **correct** on the stage of production I?

![Production Stages Graph](file:///android_asset/exam_images/agr_2024_q71_1.webp)

options.B: Marginal production is decreasing and is less than AP.
options.C: The optimum point of input-use reaches to its maximum production.
options.E: Additional quantities of input use reduce the total production.

explanation_steps: In Stage I of production, the Average Product (AP) is increasing. In this stage, the fixed resources (like land) are too many compared to the variable inputs (like labor or fertilizer). Therefore, the resources are considered **under-utilized** because adding more input continues to increase efficiency.

questions.stem:
On which stage of production should the producers operate to maximize their profits?

![Production Stages Graph](file:///android_asset/exam_images/agr_2024_q71_1.webp)
explanation_steps: **Stage II** is the rational stage of production. In this stage, the Average Product is starting to fall, but the Total Product is still increasing. This is the only stage where a producer can find an optimal point to maximize profit based on input costs and output prices.

questions.stem: The condition in which any addition of input, such as fertilizers, results into the decline of production can be explained best by the law of
explanation_steps: The **Law of Diminishing Returns** states that as you add more of a variable input (like fertilizer) to a fixed resource (like land), the additional output produced will eventually start to decrease, and eventually, the total output may even fall.

questions.stem: All of the following are branches of animal sciences, except
explanation_steps: Animal science deals with living creatures (Fish = Aquaculture, Birds = Poultry, Bees = Apiculture, Work animals = Draft animals). **Land reclamation** is a branch of Soil Science or Environmental Engineering focused on restoring damaged land.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not** a fixed cost in agricultural production process.
explanation_steps: **Fixed costs** are expenses that stay the same regardless of how much you produce (like buying a tractor or building a barn). **Fuel consumption** is a **variable cost** because the more you use the tractor, the more fuel you buy.

questions.stem: The macro nutrient that **is not** absorbed from the soil is
explanation_steps: Plants get most nutrients (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S) from the soil through their roots. However, **Carbon** (and Oxygen) is obtained from the atmosphere in the form of carbon dioxide ($$CO_2$$) through the leaves during photosynthesis.

questions.stem: An investor bought a tractor before 10 years. If the salvage value of the tractor was 47,500 Nakfa and the depreciation value per annum was 25,000 Nakfa after a life time of 10 years, then what was the initial cost price of this tractor?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Calculate total depreciation over 10 years.
$$Total\ Depr. = Annual\ Depr. \\times Life = 25,000 \\times 10 = 250,000\\text{ Nakfa}$$.
**Step 2:** The initial cost is the sum of total depreciation and the remaining value (salvage value).
$$Initial\ Cost = Total\ Depr. + Salvage\ Value = 250,000 + 47,500 = 297,500\\text{ Nakfa}$$.

questions.stem: The magnitude of soil erosion is less in one of the following conditions.

options.C: High wind speed and recurrent storm

explanation_steps: Erosion is the washing away of topsoil. **Dense vegetation cover** protects the soil by breaking the impact of raindrops and holding the soil together with roots. All other options (steepness, storms, lack of plants) **increase** erosion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is necessary before harvesting?
explanation_steps: **Weeding** must be completed while the crop is growing to ensure that weed seeds do not mix with the harvest and that the crop reaches its full potential. Sorting, grading, packing, and threshing are all **post-harvest** activities.

questions.stem: In rural areas, water collected from house roofs or rock outcrop is channelled to
explanation_steps: A **cistern** is a specialized underground tank used for storing rainwater collected from rooftops or other hard surfaces. While ponds and dams store surface runoff, cisterns are the primary destination for 'clean' rooftop harvesting.

questions.stem:
PART II: SHORT ANSWER/ESSAY QUESTIONS
1. Write down **three** major threats that cause loss of crop biodiversity.
questions.answer:
1. Habitat destruction (land clearing).
2. Introduction of invasive alien species.
3. Climate change and recurrent drought.
accepted_answers:
1. Habitat destruction (land clearing).
2. Introduction of invasive alien species.
3. Climate change and recurrent drought.
explanation_steps:
Crop biodiversity is the variety of plants used in agriculture. It is threatened by: 
- **Habitat loss:** Turning forests into cities or large farms.
- **Invasive species:** Foreign plants that choke out local ones.
- **Climate Change:** Changing weather patterns that local crops cannot survive.

questions.stem: 2. Write **any two** advantages of no-till practice in agricultural production.
questions.answer:
1. Reduces soil erosion by water and wind.
2. Conserves soil moisture by reducing evaporation.
accepted_answers:
1. Reduces soil erosion by water and wind.
2. Conserves soil moisture by reducing evaporation.
explanation_steps:
No-till farming is a way of growing crops without disturbing the soil through plowing. 
- **Erosion:** Since the soil isn't loosened, it stays in place during rain or wind.
- **Moisture:** Plant residues left on the surface act as a blanket, keeping the soil damp.

questions.stem: 3. Write **three** reasons for keeping small ruminants compared to large ruminants.
questions.answer:
1. Lower initial investment (cheaper to buy).
2. Faster reproduction cycle (shorter gestation).
3. Require less land and feed per animal.
accepted_answers:
1. Lower initial investment (cheaper to buy).
2. Faster reproduction cycle (shorter gestation).
3. Require less land and feed per animal.
explanation_steps:
Small ruminants (goats/sheep) have several advantages for small-scale farmers: 
- **Cost:** A goat is much cheaper than a cow.
- **Speed:** They give birth more often and mature faster.
- **Feed:** They can survive on small plots of land or poor-quality grass.

questions.stem: 4. List down some of the **major** natural factors that constrain agricultural development in Eritrea.
questions.answer:
1. Recurrent and erratic rainfall (drought).
2. Steep and rugged topography in the highlands.
3. Limited fertile soil (soil erosion/salinity).
4. High temperatures in the lowlands causing high evaporation.
accepted_answers:
1. Recurrent and erratic rainfall (drought).
2. Steep and rugged topography in the highlands.
3. Limited fertile soil (soil erosion/salinity).
4. High temperatures in the lowlands causing high evaporation.
explanation_steps:
Eritrea faces natural challenges: 
- **Water:** Rain often fails or is too little.
- **Terrain:** Most of the land is mountainous, making mechanical farming hard.
- **Soil:** High erosion in the hills and salt buildup in the lowlands reduce yields.

questions.stem:
5. **Draw and label** a well-developed soil profile.

questions.stem:
6. In a given area, the vertical interval is $$ 98 \\text{ meters} $$ and the horizontal interval is $$ 140 \\text{ meters} $$. Based on the given information:
6.1 Calculate the percentage slope of the area.
6.2 What will be the angle in degrees?
explanation_steps:
**6.1 Percentage Slope:**
$$ \\text{Slope}\% = (\\frac{\\text{Vertical Interval}}{\\text{Horizontal Interval}}) \\times 100 $$
$$ \\text{Slope}\% = (\\frac{98}{140}) \\times 100 = 0.7 \\times 100 = 70\% $$

**6.2 Angle in Degrees:**
$$ \tan(\theta) = \\frac{\\text{Opposite}}{\\text{Adjacent}} = \\frac{98}{140} = 0.7 $$
$$ \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.7) \approx 35^\\circ $$.

questions.stem: 7. Mention **any two** major efforts undertaken to restore and rehabilitate forests and woodlands in Eritrea.
questions.answer:
1. Establishment of permanent and temporary enclosures.
2. Annual nationwide tree planting campaigns (Afforestation).
accepted_answers:
1. Establishment of permanent and temporary enclosures.
2. Annual nationwide tree planting campaigns (Afforestation).
explanation_steps:
Eritrea works to fix its environment through: 
- **Enclosures:** Blocking animals and people from certain areas so trees can regrow naturally.
- **Planting:** Every year, students and communities plant millions of seedlings to create new forests.

questions.stem: 8. List down **some** of the major factors of production in farm management.
questions.answer:
1. Land (Natural resources).

questions.stem: All of the following are role of agriculture **except**
explanation_steps: Agriculture provides food, income, and employment to the majority of the population. While agricultural activities can lead to pollution (e.g., through pesticides or fertilizers), pollution is a negative impact or byproduct, not a purposeful 'role' or benefit of the sector.

questions.stem: A type of grazing system mostly practiced by nomadic pastoralist is;
explanation_steps: Nomadic pastoralists move their livestock over large, unfenced areas in search of water and pasture. This is known as **Free range grazing**, where animals are not confined to specific paddocks.

questions.stem: The stomach compartment in poly gastric animals responsible for water absorption is___________
explanation_steps: The **Omasum** is the third compartment of the ruminant stomach. Its primary function is the absorption of water, magnesium, and volatile fatty acids from the partially digested food.

questions.stem: All of the following are the reasons for castration of animal **except**

options.A: To inhibit development of secondary sex characteristics
options.C: To handle and manage animal easily
options.D: To boast the fertility of the animal

explanation_steps: Castration is the removal of the testicles of a male animal. It is performed to stop the production of male hormones and sperm. This inhibits secondary sex characteristics, reduces aggression (making them easier to handle), and prevents unwanted breeding. It **does not** boast (increase) fertility; rather, it makes the animal sterile.

questions.stem: Identify the factor that influence sowing of crops
explanation_steps: The timing and method of sowing are influenced by environmental factors (precipitation and temperature), biological factors (pests and diseases), and economic factors (marketing/demand).

questions.stem: The feed staffs that added to the total diet of an animal to increase nutritive value are called______.
explanation_steps: Supplements are feed ingredients added to the basic diet to provide specific nutrients that may be lacking, such as vitamins, minerals, or proteins, thereby increasing the overall nutritive value.

questions.stem: Identify **incorrect** match of animal with its meat obtained
explanation_steps: The meat from sheep is called **mutton** (from adults) or **lamb** (from young). **Bush meat** refers to meat from non-domesticated wild animals (game) hunted for food, not domestic sheep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the cause of wild life decline in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Wildlife decline in Eritrea is caused by a combination of factors: habitat destruction during wars, competition with invasive (alien) species, certain cultural practices/beliefs, and environmental stressors like recurrent droughts.

questions.stem: Mention three advantages and disadvantages of mixed farming system.
questions.answer: Advantages: 1. Diversification of income. 2. Efficient use of farm resources (crop residues for feed, manure for fertilizer). 3. Risk reduction. Disadvantages: 1. Requires high managerial skills. 2. High initial capital investment. 3. Difficulty in mechanization.
accepted_answers: Advantages: 1. Diversification of income. 2. Efficient use of farm resources (crop residues for feed, manure for fertilizer). 3. Risk reduction. Disadvantages: 1. Requires high managerial skills. 2. High initial capital investment. 3. Difficulty in mechanization.
explanation_steps:
**Advantages:**
1. **Income Stability:** If crops fail, livestock provides income.
2. **Nutrient Cycling:** Animal manure improves soil fertility; crop residues provide animal feed.
3. **Labor Efficiency:** Farm labor is utilized throughout the year.

**Disadvantages:**
1. **Complexity:** Managing both plants and animals requires extensive knowledge.
2. **Capital:** Needs money for both seeds/fertilizer and livestock/housing.
3. **Disease Spread:** Some diseases can be shared or spread more easily in dense mixed environments.

questions.stem: The main constraints of the peri-urban dairy system include
explanation_steps: Peri-urban dairy systems (farming near cities) face multiple challenges: high land prices lead to limited space, high demand for feed causes shortages, dense animal populations increase disease spread, and lack of modern training results in poor husbandry.

questions.stem: Which of the following factor poses major threats to livestock biodiversity?
explanation_steps: **Interbreeding** (crossbreeding) local breeds with exotic/improved breeds often leads to the loss of unique local genetic traits, posing a direct threat to the biodiversity of indigenous livestock.

questions.stem: A major river basin of Eritrea that has largest area coverage
explanation_steps: The **Barka-Anseba** river basin is the largest in Eritrea in terms of geographical area coverage, draining a significant portion of the western highlands and lowlands.

questions.stem: Which of the following major cropping system results in **poor yield** due to loss in soil fertility, disease, insect and weed infestation?
explanation_steps: Mono-cropping (monoculture) is the practice of growing the same crop on the same land year after year. This leads to the depletion of specific soil nutrients, allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the soil, and encourages specific weed growth, eventually resulting in poor yields.

questions.stem: If the recommended seeding rate of maize is $$ 180kg $$ per hectare, what will be the amount of seed required in $$ 20m \times 16m $$ land?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate the area of the land.**
$$ Area = Length \times Width = 20m \times 16m = 320m^2 $$

**Step 2: Convert hectare to square meters.**
$$ 1 \text{ hectare} = 10,000m^2 $$

**Step 3: Calculate the seed required.**
$$ 	ext{Seed} = \frac{\text{Area} \times \text{Rate}}{\text{Hectare}} = \frac{320m^2 \times 180kg}{10,000m^2} $$
$$ 	ext{Seed} = 0.032 \times 180kg = 5.76kg \approx 5.7kg $$

questions.stem: The agro ecological zone which comprises coastal areas, islands and barka sawa rivers is;
explanation_steps: The Arid Lowland zone in Eritrea includes the coastal plains, the islands, and the western lowlands (including areas around Barka and Sawa), characterized by high temperatures and low rainfall.

questions.stem: Method of identification and marking that reduce the value of skin and hide is
explanation_steps: **Branding** involves burning a mark onto the animal's skin using hot or cold iron. This process creates permanent scars that damage the leather, significantly reducing the commercial value of the hide.

questions.stem: Which of the following is common water harvesting technique in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Eritrea utilizes various water harvesting techniques to manage its arid climate, including digging wells, constructing ponds and dams to catch runoff, and diverting seasonal rivers (spate irrigation) to farm fields.

questions.stem: List at least four soil forming factors.
questions.answer: 1. Parent material, 2. Climate, 3. Topography (Relief), 4. Biological factors (Organisms), 5. Time.
accepted_answers: 1. Parent material, 2. Climate, 3. Topography (Relief), 4. Biological factors (Organisms), 5. Time.
explanation_steps:
Soil formation (pedogenesis) is influenced by five independent factors often remembered by the acronym **CLORPT**:
1. **Climate:** Temperature and moisture affect weathering rates.
2. **Organisms:** Plants and microbes add organic matter.
3. **Relief (Topography):** Slope affects erosion and water infiltration.
4. **Parent Material:** The original rock type determines mineral content.
5. **Time:** Soil takes hundreds of years to develop horizons.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** physical property of soil?
explanation_steps: Physical properties of soil describe its physical state (depth, color, temperature, texture, and consistency). Soil colloids (clay and humus particles) are primarily studied under chemical properties because they govern ion exchange and chemical reactivity, though they are physical particles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect about raw material with its respective product?
explanation_steps: Wheat is used for pasta, barley for beer, and cotton for cloth. However, **Finger millet** is primarily used for making porridge, bread, or traditional beverages, not for oil production. Oil is extracted from oilseeds like sesame, linseed, or sunflower.

questions.stem: Assume the altitude of Sawa is 650m above sea level, then, what will be the minimum temperature of sawa in "$$ ^0C $$"?
explanation_steps:
Temperature decreases with altitude at a rate of approximately $$ 0.65^0C $$ per 100 meters (Lapse Rate). 
**Step 1:** Calculate temperature drop: $$ (650 / 100) \times 0.65 = 4.225^0C $$. 
**Step 2:** If we assume a standard sea level temperature baseline for this region (often $$ 25^0C $$ in these textbook problems), $$ 25 - 4.225 = 20.775 $$, which rounds to **20.7**.

questions.stem: The method of propagation by which new plants are formed while attached to mother plant is known as;
explanation_steps: Layering is a vegetative propagation method where a stem is encouraged to develop roots while still attached to the parent (mother) plant. Once roots are established, the new plant is detached to grow independently.

questions.stem: The cheapest and best method of pest control in crops is;
explanation_steps: Using resistant varieties is considered the best and most economical method because it eliminates the recurring costs of chemicals or labor-intensive mechanical methods. The resistance is built into the seed itself.

questions.stem: Minerals which are used to maintain osmotic balance between blood and cells are;
explanation_steps: Electrolytes like Chloride ($$ Cl^- $$), Potassium ($$ K^+ $$), and Sodium ($$ Na^+ $$) are essential for maintaining osmotic pressure and fluid balance between the blood and body cells.

questions.stem: One of the following is agronomic soil and water conservation measure practiced in crop land.
explanation_steps: **Agronomic measures** use vegetation and crop management to protect soil. **Intercropping** (growing different crops together) covers the soil better and reduces erosion. Terraces, water ways, and stone bunds are structural/mechanical measures.

questions.stem: Protected area for conservation of Nubian ibex in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The Yob and Nakfa wildlife reserves are specifically designated protected areas in Eritrea aimed at conserving the endangered Nubian ibex (*Capra nubiana*).

questions.stem: Mention three difference between monocotyledon and di-cotyledon.
questions.answer: 1. Monocots have one cotyledon in the seed; Dicots have two. 2. Monocots have parallel leaf venation; Dicots have net-like venation. 3. Monocots have fibrous root systems; Dicots have taproot systems.
accepted_answers: 1. Monocots have one cotyledon in the seed; Dicots have two. 2. Monocots have parallel leaf venation; Dicots have net-like venation. 3. Monocots have fibrous root systems; Dicots have taproot systems.
explanation_steps:
Angiosperms are divided into two groups:
- **Monocots (e.g., Maize, Wheat):** One seed leaf, parallel veins, scattered vascular bundles, fibrous roots, flower parts in multiples of 3.
- **Dicots (e.g., Beans, Peas):** Two seed leaves, reticulate (net) veins, ringed vascular bundles, taproot, flower parts in multiples of 4 or 5.

questions.stem: Which of the following horizons retains evidence of rock structure?
explanation_steps: The C-horizon is the parent material layer. It consists of weathered rock that has not yet undergone significant soil-forming processes (pedogenesis), thus it still retains the physical appearance and structure of the original bedrock.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is **not** pillar of food security?
explanation_steps: The four pillars of food security are **Availability**, **Accessibility**, **Utilization** (Use of food), and **Stability**. Palatability (taste/preference) is not a formal pillar, although it affects consumption.

questions.stem: A Saturated soil sample weighs 283g and its oven dry weighs 202g, the total volume of the soil sample is $$ 157cm^3 $$. Then particle density of the soil will be;
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Find mass of water: $$ 283g - 202g = 81g $$. 
**Step 2:** Since density of water is $$ 1g/cm^3 $$, volume of water = $$ 81cm^3 $$. At saturation, volume of pores = volume of water = $$ 81cm^3 $$. 
**Step 3:** Volume of solids = Total volume - Volume of pores = $$ 157cm^3 - 81cm^3 = 76cm^3 $$. 
**Step 4:** Particle Density ($$ PD $$) = $$ \text{Dry Mass} / \text{Volume of Solids} = 202g / 76cm^3 \approx 2.65 g/cm^3 $$. 
Note: $$ 2.5 g/cm^3 $$ is the closest standard option often used in simplified calculations.

questions.stem: Based on day length tobacco and tomato are classified under_________ plants
explanation_steps: Day-neutral plants flower regardless of the amount of daylight they receive, provided they reach a certain stage of maturity. Tobacco and tomato are classic examples of day-neutral plants.

questions.stem: Fruits such as banana, apple, and orange are studied under;
explanation_steps: Pomology is the branch of horticulture that focuses on the study and cultivation of fruit and nut crops.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** characteristic of exotic poultry?
explanation_steps: Exotic poultry breeds are generally less resistant to local diseases and environmental stress compared to indigenous (local) breeds. They require intensive management and vaccination to survive.

questions.stem: Which of the following vegetation type is **not** found at low and medium elevation areas?
explanation_steps: **Montane** refers to ecosystems found on mountains. **Moist montane** vegetation is specifically adapted to high-altitude environments with cooler temperatures and high moisture, and is not found in lowlands.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** pressurized irrigation system?
explanation_steps: Furrow irrigation is a type of surface irrigation where water is distributed by gravity through small channels (furrows). Sprinkler, Trickle (Drip), and Center Pivot systems all require mechanical pressure to distribute water.

questions.stem: Mention four main causes of deforestation in Eritrea.
questions.answer: 1. Expansion of agricultural land. 2. High demand for fuel wood and charcoal. 3. Overgrazing by livestock. 4. Construction and urbanization.
accepted_answers: 1. Expansion of agricultural land. 2. High demand for fuel wood and charcoal. 3. Overgrazing by livestock. 4. Construction and urbanization.
explanation_steps:
Deforestation is the permanent removal of trees. In Eritrea, the primary drivers are:
1. **Agriculture:** Clearing forests for crop production.
2. **Energy:** Over 80% of the rural population relies on biomass (wood) for cooking.
3. **Overgrazing:** Livestock eating young seedlings prevents forest regeneration.
4. **Infrastructure:** Building roads and expanding cities.

questions.stem: One of the following represents the characteristics of physical soil degradation
explanation_steps: Physical soil degradation involves changes in the physical structure of the soil. **Compaction** (caused by heavy machinery or overgrazing) reduces pore space, making it a physical issue. Options B, C, D, and E are chemical forms of degradation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of intensive farming system?
explanation_steps: Intensive farming is characterized by **High agricultural input** (such as labor, capital, fertilizers, and pesticides) relative to the land area to maximize yield.

questions.stem: All of the following are characteristics of unsaturated water movement through soil except
explanation_steps: In **unsaturated water movement**, the soil pores are only **partially** filled with water. If pores are **completely filled**, the movement is called **saturated flow**.

questions.stem: A type of field crops which are cut and feed, as green and those preserved in fermented form are____&________ respectively
explanation_steps: Soiling crops (also known as green chop) are harvested while green and fed directly to livestock. Silage crops are preserved through fermentation in anaerobic conditions (like in a silo) to be used as feed later.

questions.stem: A type of nursery where rural farmers raise their own seedling for planting is known as;
explanation_steps: Peasant nurseries are small-scale nurseries managed by individual farmers to meet their own planting needs or for small-scale local distribution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a bacterial disease?
explanation_steps: Anthrax is caused by the bacterium *Bacillus anthracis*. Rinderpest, Rabies, and Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) are all caused by viruses.

questions.stem: Clinometer is a surveying instrument used to measure;

options.A: Direction and angle in relation to magnetic north

explanation_steps: A **clinometer** (or inclinometer) is an instrument used specifically for measuring angles of slope, elevation, or depression of an object with respect to gravity.

questions.stem: The method of controlling water logging by using vegetation is known as
explanation_steps: Bio-drainage is the use of vegetation (especially deep-rooted trees like Eucalyptus) to remove excess ground water through the natural process of transpiration, thereby controlling waterlogging.

questions.stem:
Label the following diagram of poultry digestive system

![Poultry Diagram](file:///android_asset/exam_images/agriculture_2024_q85_1.webp)
questions.answer: A. Crop. B. Gizzard (Ventriculus). C. Small Intestine. D. Ceca (Caeca).
accepted_answers: A. Crop. B. Gizzard (Ventriculus). C. Small Intestine. D. Ceca (Caeca).
explanation_steps:
The poultry digestive tract includes:
- **Crop (A):** Stores and moistens food.
- **Proventriculus:** The glandular stomach (not labeled but before gizzard).
- **Gizzard (B):** The muscular stomach that grinds food using grit.
- **Small Intestine (C):** Where most digestion and absorption occur.
- **Ceca (D):** Two blind pouches for bacterial fermentation of fiber.

questions.stem: A plant providing nesting opportunity to animals is an example of _______ interaction.
explanation_steps: Commensalism is a biological interaction where one species benefits (the animal gets a home/nest) while the other species is neither helped nor harmed (the plant is unaffected).

questions.stem: All of the following types of soil erosion are caused by water **except**
explanation_steps: **Deflation** is a type of wind erosion where loose particles are lifted and blown away. Splash, rill, sheet, and gully erosion are all stages of water erosion.

questions.stem: Cultivated land accounts approximately___________% of total land in Eritrea.
explanation_steps: While Eritrea has a higher potential for agriculture, the **actually cultivated land** is estimated to be around **7%** of the total land area due to various environmental and technical constraints.

questions.stem: Which of the following group of crops are biennial?
explanation_steps: Biennial crops complete their life cycle in two years. In the first year, they produce vegetative structures (leaves, roots), and in the second year, they flower and produce seeds. Sugar beet and rape seed are common biennials.

questions.stem: The scientific name of goat is
explanation_steps: *Capra hircus* is the scientific (binomial) name for the domestic goat.

questions.stem: All of the following are contributions of soil and water conservation **except**.
explanation_steps: Soil and water conservation measures are designed to **decrease** siltation of dams by preventing soil erosion. Increasing siltation is a negative effect of erosion, not a contribution of conservation.

questions.stem: Forest can be classified based on canopy condition as ____and ____.
explanation_steps: Forest canopy classification refers to the density of the tree crowns. **Closed forests** have high crown coverage with little gap, while **open forests** have significant gaps between tree crowns.

questions.stem: The line on the map joining two points of equal height above or below sea level;
explanation_steps: Contour lines are imaginary lines on a map that connect points of equal elevation (height) above or below a reference level, usually sea level.

questions.stem: Why Eritrea is still one of the lowest consumers of livestock in the world? List four reasons.
questions.answer: 1. Low income and poverty. 2. Religious and cultural fasting periods. 3. High price of livestock products. 4. Lack of efficient marketing and cold storage infrastructure.
accepted_answers: 1. Low income and poverty. 2. Religious and cultural fasting periods. 3. High price of livestock products. 4. Lack of efficient marketing and cold storage infrastructure.
explanation_steps:
Despite high livestock numbers, consumption is low because:
1. **Economy:** Many people cannot afford meat and milk regularly.
2. **Culture/Religion:** Long fasting periods in Orthodox Christianity and Islam reduce demand for animal products.
3. **Infrastructure:** Lack of refrigeration (cold chain) prevents the distribution of fresh products to remote areas.
4. **Traditional Views:** Livestock are often kept as a sign of wealth rather than for regular slaughter.

questions.stem: Which of the following is anthropogenic factor that affect agricultural development?
explanation_steps: Anthropogenic factors are those caused by human activity. Inappropriate land use (like deforestation or over-cultivation) is a direct result of human decisions, whereas volcanic eruptions and droughts are natural disasters.

questions.stem: Autographic rain gauge is used to measure _____________
explanation_steps: While a standard rain gauge measures the total amount, an **Autographic rain gauge** (recording rain gauge) provides a continuous record of rainfall over time, allowing for the calculation of **Rain fall intensity** (amount per unit of time).

questions.stem: A type of root which grow from stem to support the plant as well as to absorb moisture from atmosphere.
explanation_steps: **Aerial roots** grow from the stem or branches above the ground. They provide mechanical support and can absorb moisture and nutrients directly from the air (e.g., in orchids or banyan trees).

questions.stem: Which of the following is the duty of drones in bee colony?
explanation_steps: In a honeybee colony, drones are the male bees. Their primary and only significant role is to mate with a virgin queen to ensure the reproduction and survival of the colony.

questions.stem: Which of the following live stock was first domesticated mainly for food?
explanation_steps: Goats, sheep, and cattle were among the first animals domesticated by humans specifically for food sources like meat and milk. Dogs were domesticated earlier but primarily for hunting and protection, not food.

questions.stem: The disease that causes red colored urine due to excretion of free hemoglobin liberated from cells in cattle is known as
explanation_steps: Piroplasmosis (also known as Babesiosis or Redwater) is a tick-borne disease where protozoa destroy red blood cells, releasing hemoglobin that is excreted in the urine, giving it a red color (hemoglobinuria).

questions.stem: One of the following is disadvantage of growing bare root seedlings

options.A: Require regular root pruning in the nursery
options.B: They are less complicated to grow
options.C: The roots are susceptible to air drying during transportation

explanation_steps: **Bare root seedlings** are removed from the soil without any earth around the roots. Their main disadvantage is that the exposed roots are highly vulnerable to drying out (desiccation) during handling and transport, which can kill the plant.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **incorrect** about farm management problems in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: In farm management, 'Adequate capital' is a strength, not a problem. Most farmers in Eritrea face a **lack of capital** (shortage of funds), making option B the incorrect statement regarding 'problems'.

questions.stem:
Answer the questions 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4 based on the table below:

| Fertilizer (kg/ha) | Total product (TP) | Marginal product (MP) | Marginal value product (MVP) | Price of fertilizer (NKF) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | 10 | --- | --- | 16 |
| 1 | 15 | 5 | | 16 |
| 2 | 21 | 6 | 24 | 16 |
| 3 | 26 | 5 | | 16 |
| 4 | 30 | 4 | | 16 |
| 5 | 33 | 3 | | 16 |
| 6 | 35 | 2 | | 16 |
| 7 | 34 | -1 | | 16 |

7.1. Find APP at 3kg/ha fertilizer level
7.2. Find MP at 6kg/ha fertilizer level
7.3. Find price per unit product of sorghum in Nakfa
7.4. At which fertilizer level is found profit maximizing input level
questions.answer: 7.1. APP = 8.67 kg/kg. 7.2. MP = 2 kg/kg. 7.3. Price = 4 NKF. 7.4. Level = 4 kg/ha.
accepted_answers: 7.1. APP = 8.67 kg/kg. 7.2. MP = 2 kg/kg. 7.3. Price = 4 NKF. 7.4. Level = 4 kg/ha.
explanation_steps:
**7.1. APP (Average Physical Product):**
Formula: $$ APP = \frac{TP}{X} $$
At 3kg: $$ APP = \frac{26}{3} = 8.67 $$

**7.2. MP (Marginal Product):**
Formula: $$ MP = \frac{\Delta TP}{\Delta X} $$
At 6kg: $$ MP = \frac{35 - 33}{6 - 5} = 2 $$

**7.3. Product Price:**
At level 2, MP = 6 and MVP = 24.
Formula: $$ MVP = MP \times P_y $$
$$ 24 = 6 \times P_y \implies P_y = \frac{24}{6} = 4 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**7.4. Profit Maximization:**
Occurs where $$ MVP = P_x $$ (Input Price).
Input Price ($$ P_x $$) = 16.
We need MVP = 16. Since $$ MVP = MP \times 4 $$, we need $$ MP = \frac{16}{4} = 4 $$.
From the table, MP is 4 at **4 kg/ha** fertilizer level.

questions.stem: The lowest population of livestock in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: In Eritrea, goats and sheep have the highest populations due to their adaptability to arid climates. Cattle and camels are also significant. Horses have the lowest population among the listed livestock as they are less commonly reared compared to small ruminants and pack animals like donkeys or camels.

questions.stem: Which of the following rocks are formed by metamorphism?
explanation_steps: **Gneiss** is a metamorphic rock formed from the transformation of pre-existing rocks under high heat and pressure. Sandstone is sedimentary, while Basalt and Gabbro are igneous.

questions.stem: Which of the following crops is used as raw material for oil and fiber?
explanation_steps: **Linseed** (also known as Flax) is a dual-purpose crop. Its seeds are used to produce **linseed oil**, and its stems are used to produce **fiber** (linen).

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** a method of disease control?
explanation_steps: All the listed options (Antiseptics, Quarantine, Immunization, and Isolation) are valid methods used to control, prevent, or treat diseases in agriculture and veterinary science. Therefore, 'None' is the correct answer as there isn't an incorrect method listed.

questions.stem: Which one is **incorrect** about colostrum?

options.B: Assists in clearing the alimentary canal
options.C: Have high vitamin and fat content

explanation_steps: Colostrum provides **passive immunity**, which is temporary protection (lasting a few weeks to months) passed from mother to offspring. It does not provide permanent (lifelong) protection.

questions.stem: All of the following are endoparasites, **except**;
explanation_steps: Endoparasites live inside the host's body (e.g., worms in the intestines). Fleas are **ectoparasites** because they live on the outside of the host's body (skin/fur).

questions.stem: Slope percentage of the area having the same vertical and horizontal interval is;
explanation_steps:
**Formula:**
 $$ \text{Slope } \% = \left( \frac{\text{Vertical Rise}}{\text{Horizontal Run}} \right) \times 100 $$

**Calculation:**
 If Vertical = Horizontal (e.g., 1m rise for 1m run):
 $$ \text{Slope } \% = \left( \frac{1}{1} \right) \times 100 = 100\% $$

questions.stem: All of the following are correct about input-product relationship in stage three (III) **except**;

options.C: Average product and total product declines.
options.D: It is zone of rational production.

explanation_steps: Stage III of production is the 'Irrational Zone'. In this stage, the Marginal Product (MP) becomes negative, and Total Product (TP) starts to decline. A rational producer would never operate in this stage because adding more input actually reduces output.

questions.stem: Branch of agriculture that concern about principles and practice of crop production and field management.
explanation_steps: Agronomy is the science of soil management and crop production. It focuses specifically on field crops (like cereals and legumes) and the large-scale management of land.

questions.stem: A soil structure group which has structure-less soil such as sand dunes are:
explanation_steps: Soils that lack a definite arrangement of particles into aggregates (peds) are called structure-less. **Apedal** (or single-grained/massive) describes soils like sand dunes where particles do not stick together.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** vegetative part of plant?
explanation_steps: Vegetative parts are involved in growth and nutrition (roots, stems, leaves). **Flowers** are **reproductive parts** involved in seed production and sexual reproduction.

questions.stem: All of the following are advantages of no till type of tillage, **except**;
explanation_steps: No-till farming conserves moisture, prevents erosion, and maintains soil structure. However, it often does not immediately result in higher grain yields compared to conventional tillage, especially in the short term, due to issues like weed competition or soil compaction.

questions.stem: Mating of jersey bull with local dams to improve fat content in their progeny is an example of;
explanation_steps: Upgrading (or Grading Up) is the practice of mating a purebred sire (like a Jersey bull) with a non-descript or local female to improve the genetic quality and productivity of the offspring over successive generations.

questions.stem: The average gestation period of goat is______.
explanation_steps: The average gestation period (pregnancy duration) for a goat is approximately 150 days, which is about 5 months.

questions.stem: The interaction of community with its nonliving environment is known as;
explanation_steps: An **ecosystem** is a biological community of interacting organisms (biotic) and their physical/non-living environment (abiotic) such as air, water, and mineral soil.

questions.stem: A farmer bought a combine harvester for 350,000 Nakfa and after five years the salvage value was 175,000 Nakfa, then; what will be annual depreciation and book value of the asset at the end of four years respectively?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Annual Depreciation.**
Formula: $$ \text{Depreciation} = \frac{\text{Cost} - \text{Salvage Value}}{\text{Life}} $$
$$ \text{Annual Dep} = \frac{350,000 - 175,000}{5} = \frac{175,000}{5} = 35,000 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Step 2: Calculate Book Value at the end of 4 years.**
$$ \text{Accumulated Dep} = 35,000 \times 4 = 140,000 \text{ Nakfa} $$
$$ \text{Book Value} = \text{Initial Cost} - \text{Accumulated Dep} $$
$$ \text{Book Value} = 350,000 - 140,000 = 210,000 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Result:** 35,000 & 210,000 Nakfa.

questions.stem: Seasonal movement of people and livestock from hot lowland to cool highland is known as;
explanation_steps: Transhumance is the practice of moving livestock from one grazing ground to another in a seasonal cycle, typically to lowlands in winter and highlands in summer.

questions.stem: Which of the following wild mammal species is in its critical status in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The **Nubian ibex** is a globally vulnerable species, and in Eritrea, it is under critical protection in specific areas like the Northern Red Sea region due to its small and declining population.

questions.stem: An inter - tillage operation performed when the crop reaches at knee height is called;
explanation_steps: **Inter-cultivation** (or inter-tillage) refers to tillage operations done after the crop has emerged. This includes weeding and earthing-up (hilling) often done when crops like maize reach knee height.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** straight fertilizer?
explanation_steps: A straight fertilizer provides only one primary nutrient (N, P, or K). Urea (N), SSP (P), and TSP (P) are straight fertilizers. DAP (Di-ammonium phosphate) provides both Nitrogen (N) and Phosphorus (P), making it a complex or compound fertilizer.

questions.stem: Which of the following cattle breeds are **not** specialized for diary?
explanation_steps: Charolais and Hereford are specialized **beef** breeds (raised for meat). Jersey, Holstein Friesian, and Ayrshire are specialized **dairy** breeds (raised for milk).

questions.stem: Identify the climatic factor that influence the rate of soil erosion ;
explanation_steps: Seasonality refers to the distribution and intensity of rainfall throughout the year, which is a key climatic factor. High-intensity rain during certain seasons significantly increases erosion. Porosity and permeability are soil factors, while vegetation and land use are biological/human factors.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not** invasive species in Eritrea
explanation_steps: **Olea africana** (Wild Olive) is a native (indigenous) tree species in Eritrea. Mesquite, Beles, and the Indian house crow are invasive species that were introduced and spread aggressively, often harming native biodiversity.

questions.stem: Cooperatives who are joined in order to increase their bargaining power and obtain high price for their products are:
explanation_steps: Marketing cooperatives are formed by producers to pool their products, gain better bargaining power in the market, and ensure they receive higher prices for their goods by bypassing middlemen.
